answer: Urban land use is most strongly associated with **Unintentional** (accidental/contaminant) introductions: the Unintentional pathway is the one most tightly coupled to urban cover (Spearman r ≈ +0.50, p < 10⁻⁴⁰ across all 632 plots), and in the 191 invaded plots urban land use roughly triples the odds that Unintentional introductions dominate the invaded species (adjusted OR ≈ 3.2; unadjusted OR ≈ 2.4, p ≈ 0.01). **Gardening** (ornamental) introductions are also linked to urban land use but in the opposite compositional direction — their raw counts rise with urban cover (Spearman ≈ +0.40) yet their relative share among invaded species is lower in more urban plots (adjusted OR ≈ 0.29, p ≈ 0.04). **AgriForest** introductions show no detectable, stable urban effect (null in the adjusted count and composition models), but with only 23 AgriForest species this null is underpowered rather than definitive.

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use is most strongly associated with Unintentional (accidental/contaminant) introductions: the Unintentional pathway is the one most tightly coupled to urban cover (Spearman r ~ +0.50, p < 1e-40 across all 632 plots), and in the 191 invaded plots urban land use roughly triples the odds that Unintentional introductions dominate the invaded species (adjusted OR ~ 3.2; unadjusted OR ~ 2.4, p ~ 0.01). Gardening (ornamental) introductions are also linked to urban land use but in the opposite compositional direction: their raw counts rise with urban cover (Spearman ~ +0.40) yet their relative share among invaded species is lower in more urban plots (adjusted OR ~ 0.29, p ~ 0.04). AgriForest introductions show no detectable, stable urban effect (null in the adjusted count and composition models), but with only 23 AgriForest species this null is underpowered rather than definitive.
payload.workflow: Unit of observation = plot (the 632 rows of invaded_niche_pathways.csv, the only file with both per-plot pathway counts n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo and urban land-cover variables; the species-level, temporal, and phylogenetic files were not needed for this land-cover question). (1) Marginal picture: Spearman/Pearson of each pathway count vs urban.2009.500m plus unadjusted negative-binomial GLMs. (2) Primary model: negative-binomial GLM (NB2 dispersion alpha estimated by profile likelihood) for each pathway count ~ urban.2009.500m + covariates (habitat[10], elevation, cropland.2009.500m, distance.road, distance.stream, annual.temperature, annual.rainfall); urban coefficient, 95% CI, and p reported. (3) Sensitivity: same model refit with urban.2009.50m, urban.2009.1000m, urban.1993.500m, and the 1993->2009 progressive-urban change term. (4) Spatial check: Moran's I on NB residuals (k-NN k=10, 999 permutations); n.s. for all pathways, so no spatial correction applied. (5) Composition: binomial GLM (n.pathway out of n.total) on the 191 invaded plots ~ urban.2009.500m + covariates (and unadjusted), to test which pathway type dominates invaded species as urbanization rises. A habitat diagnostic shows the 'Urban' habitat (mean 57% urban cover, highest invasion, Unintentional-dominant) drives the marginal urban->count correlation, explaining why the adjusted count model attenuates.
